invention.author_prose:
In the hotel_suite_large bedroom, the wearer begins by saying, “I’m tidying before checkout. I usually keep the travel folder on the bedroom desk, but I may set it down while I clear things. When I ask for it, help me find the last place you actually saw it so I can bring it back to the desk.”

At the start, the folder is on the bedroom shelf, the desk is clear enough to receive it, a clipboard is on the desk, a hand towel is on one bathroom shelf, and an apple is on the bedroom shelf. The wearer walks to the bedroom shelf, picks up the folder, and puts it on the bedroom desk, reinforcing the obvious and habitual location. They then pick up the clipboard from the desk and put it on the bedroom shelf while continuing to tidy.

A little later, the wearer picks the folder up from the bedroom desk, walks into bathroom_0, and puts the folder on one of the bathroom shelves while freeing a hand. This is the last observed location of the folder. The wearer then does several unrelated but goal-consistent tidying actions: picks up the hand towel from the other bathroom shelf, walks back to the bedroom, puts the towel on the bedroom shelf, picks up the apple from the bedroom shelf, and puts the apple on the desk. By now the camera view is back in the bedroom, where the desk is visible with the apple but not the folder; the bathroom shelf is no longer in view.

The wearer asks, “Where did I leave the travel folder? I need it back on the bedroom desk.” The assistant should answer from the latest observed evidence: the folder was last seen on the bathroom shelf after it was removed from the bedroom desk. It should direct the wearer to go to bathroom_0, pick up the folder from that shelf, return to the bedroom, and put it on the desk.

A weak assistant fails by relying on the stated habit and the earlier repeated desk sighting, telling the wearer to look on the bedroom desk. That answer leaves the wearer searching the wrong place or failing to retrieve it. Success is the folder being retrieved from the bathroom shelf and placed on the bedroom desk; failure is acting on the older habitual location instead of the most recent observed one.

capability.boundary: The answer is the last supported location, not the most common location and not a generic search guess.
capability.few_shot: Across one day in a house, a pair of reading glasses appears by the bed, in the bathroom, twice on the kitchen counter, later on the sofa, and finally at 15:00 on the study desk. An empty glasses case remains on the kitchen counter as a strong habitual-location decoy. At dusk the wearer asks where the glasses are. The assistant must retrieve the latest sighting in the study, guide the wearer there, and have the glasses placed in the case afterward. Choosing the kitchen because it appeared most often is the characteristic failure. The scored outcome is the reading glasses inside their case after retrieval.
capability.target: Retrieve an object's most recent observed location while resisting a habitual or frequently seen location that is no longer current.
